title: Parties implicated in a proposal's outcome must be shown the exact wording used to describe their item
content:
A.1.10.2.4.8.3.7 closes with a duty that is easy to skim past: "The Core Facilitator must also make sure that the parties implicated in the proposal outcome are aware of the wording used for each item in the Executive Document."

This is distinct from the Content Liaison confirmations at A.1.10.2.4.5.3, which cover derived-cell specifics — addresses, amounts, parameter values — in the Executive Sheet. Here the object is the *prose* in the public document, and the concern is characterization rather than correctness.

The gap it closes is real. An item can carry entirely accurate figures and still be described in a way that misrepresents its purpose, invites a hostile reading, or omits the context that makes it reasonable. Numbers are confirmable by the parties who supplied them; framing is only checkable by the party whose activity is being framed.

Because the Executive Document is the artifact voters actually read, its wording — not the Executive Sheet's — is what shapes the outcome and the ecosystem's perception of the affected party. Giving implicated parties advance sight makes the framing contestable before publication rather than after, when the vote is already in progress and correction is costly.

The obligation is deliberately weak — awareness, not approval. Affected parties get no veto over how their item is described, which keeps the Core Facilitator's editorial independence intact while removing the excuse of surprise.
description: A.1.10.2.4.8.3.7 adds a pre-publication sight requirement beyond value confirmation, so an affected party can object to a characterization, not just to a number.
